note: SEVENTH SPP KEEPER, PROMOTED 2026-09-10 (lane SPP-62) over keeper 6 (lane SPP-61) BY OWNER RULING in-session, verbatim: 'Is this a recommended keeper candidate? If so plz promote. If structural integrity improves but gates regress that may still be a keeper.' THE RUN: keeper 6's recipe plus EXACTLY ONE change, and it is a DATA-INPUT repair, not a model change -- the R-ay coal supply-class census now reads the solved span's own EIA-860 releases (scripts/data/derive_coal_supply.py --census-vintage 2023 2024 2025), so coal_supply_SPP.csv carries 31 rows instead of 29. NO ScenarioConfig field, no shared default, no new tunable, and NOT ONE LINE of solve-path code under src/. Solved as ONE --years 2023 2024 2025 invocation, years sequential (rules 12 / 16 [R-ALLYEARS]), 440 s wall. WHAT IT CLOSES: A SCORING BLIND SPOT, NOT A RESIDUAL. Keeper 6 books 4.3551 TWh (2023) and 2.0670 TWh (2024) of coal dispatch in a BARE 'COAL' CLASS THE SPP EIA-923 BENCHMARK HAS NO ROW FOR -- re-scored at HEAD, that energy appears in NO C1 row, passing or failing, so it is scored against NOTHING and COAL_PRB reads low by exactly the missing amount. This is the defect SPP-61's own FINDING section 4 root-caused and routed as successor card R-ay ('a PREREQUISITE, not an alternative'); keeper 6 was promoted before it landed. The cause: derive_coal_supply.py built its coal census from load_fleet_from_csv with NO VINTAGE -- the canonical 2025 Early Release, in which Harrington (6193) reads NG -- for every solved year, so the plant was absent from the census, got no rank, fell through all four resolver steps to '' and landed in bare COAL. EIA-923 reports fuel code SUB for 6193 in 2023 and 2024, which maps to COAL_PRB; the model now reaches the SAME CLASS THE BENCHMARK DOES, which is the identity SPP-61's gate G3 tested and failed. THE SINGLE-DELTA A/B AGAINST KEEPER 6 IS AS CLEAN AS THESE GET: in 2023, 4.3551 TWh moves from COAL to COAL_PRB and NOTHING ELSE -- all fourteen other classes byte-identical to four decimals (ST_GAS 7.0867, CT_PEAKER 16.2967, CC_REGULAR 42.4877, COAL_LIGNITE 7.2935, wind 113.7572, ...). In 2024 the same re-label moves 2.0670 TWh. That doubles as a stronger G-DRIFT corroboration than a hunk audit: the 21 files changed between keeper 6's basis and this run's base are MEASURABLY inert for SPP. THE GATES ARE A WASH AND ONE ROW MOVES THE WRONG WAY -- REPORTED AT FULL MAGNITUDE, NEVER ABSORBED. DETERMINATION NOT-YET on both, on the IDENTICAL basis (fuelmix, price_tail); grade 6 of 8 on both; 0 caveats of any kind on both; free-class C1 14/16 all / 10/12 free on both. Exactly TWO scored rows move, in OPPOSITE directions: 2023 COAL_PRB 62.522 -> 66.877 against 65.279 actual, i.e. -2.76 -> +1.60 TWh, absolute error DOWN 1.16 TWh; and 2024 COAL_PRB 59.651 -> 61.718 against 59.953 actual, i.e. -0.30 -> +1.76 TWh, absolute error UP 1.46 TWh. Both stay inside the +/-8.00 TWh band. Keeper 6's near-perfect 2024 coal row was an ARTIFACT of the blind spot -- it read -0.30 only because 2.067 TWh sat in an unscorable class -- so the apparent accuracy was luck, not fidelity; the degradation is real all the same and is stated here rather than explained away. C2 / C3a / C3b / C3c / C4 / C6 / C8 are UNCHANGED, every row. WHAT ELSE IMPROVES, both reported rather than gating: C5a system CO2 (REPORTED-ONLY, rubric v2.9, contributes no status) more than HALVES its error in both scored years, -5.6 / -3.1 / +2.9 % -> -1.7 / -1.2 / +2.9 %, which is independent physical evidence that the classification repair makes the model more faithful and not merely more legible; and C8 forced-share gains two measurable rows (COAL 2023 / 2024 SKIPPED -> PASS at 0.0 % forced) that keeper 6 could not score at all. WHAT THIS KEEPER DOES NOT FIX, stated so no reader infers otherwise: SPP IS NOT CALIBRATED and this promotion moves the scoreboard NOWHERE. Both ST_GAS C1 rows still FAIL (2023 -8.38 TWh, 2024 -9.71 TWh, identical to keeper 6 -- the census repair touches coal classification, not gas dispatch) and C3c still fails in all three years (model 0 / 5 / 0 hours above $200 against 42 / 59 / 68 actual). Because TWO criteria fail, the rule 22 [R-C3C] standing rule cannot fire: it requires a LONE failure. The named successor is UNCHANGED from keeper 6 -- the ST_GAS offer / commitment defect, model ST_GAS already 6.95 / 8.13 TWh below actual BEFORE either repair -- and keeper 5's other structural objects are all still open: the thermal-commitment floor (the LP absorbs 98.2 % of concentrated curtailment headroom; thermal annual minimum 254.3 MW across a ~40 GW fleet), the zonal spread (measured |N-S| 12.13 / 17.23 / 15.18 against a model ~1), and the absent scarcity mechanism (SPP-55/56). RULE 23 [R-FROZEN-DERIVE] -- THE CRUX, AND THE ARGUMENT STANDS WITHOUT THE RESIDUAL. The cited trigger is a change in the DERIVE'S OWN INPUT (its plant census read an EIA-860 registry measured wrong for the solved year, and the correct release was already committed on disk), NOT a residual that moved. Three facts carry it: (a) the rank is not a choice -- SUB -> prb at 100 % of ranked weight, 26,193,400.3 MWh for 6193 and 156,101.0 MWh for 10862, by the same arithmetic that ranks the other 29 plants; (b) the repair is INERT for every committed run -- all seven ISOs' fleets byte-identical field-for-field, and 46 of 46 committed run_configs read the canonical registry; (c) it moves the target residual the WRONG way, which a fitted change does not do. The --year span is untouched, so the PRE-PATCH script reproduces the committed CSV BYTE-IDENTICALLY (md5 5a71bd95bf10a732af980086e541ffa3) -- that anchor is what makes the impact census exact: ALL 29 INCUMBENT ROWS BYTE-IDENTICAL, the re-derive being 2 insertions(+) and 0 deletions. Not luck: the census is a MEMBERSHIP FILTER and each plant's rank is computed from its own EIA-923 rows independent of every other plant, so widening it can only ADD rows. RULE 19 [R-ONE-MECH]: no fifth resolver. Both new plants were unresolved by ALL FOUR existing steps, so no existing resolution changes hands -- 7902 Pirkey keeps its retiree-fallback lignite and 57937 stays unresolved (both are coal only in vintage_2020, outside the solved span). RULE 21 [R-DOF]: ledger INHERITED VERBATIM from keeper 6, n_entries 3 and n_residual 2, because the repair sets no value. Keeper 5's authorized_price_tuning block (offer_curve_by_group 0.93 on all four bands of the ten registered fossil classes, rules 1 / 13 amendment 2026-09-05) is replayed VERBATIM, was NOT re-cut by this lane, and no multiplier was swept against any gate. RULE 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE]: derive_coal_supply.py is SHARED, so the new --census-vintage argument DEFAULTS to the canonical snapshot alone -- the historical construction. MEASURED: with the patch applied and no flag passed, SPP / PJM / MISO / NEISO all re-derive BYTE-IDENTICALLY to the pre-patch script at HEAD, so no ISO's CSV moves unless deliberately re-derived. Plant codes 6193 and 10862 appear in SPP's fleet ONLY (3 and 1 generators) and in NO other ISO's fleet, even though _derived_coal_supply globs every ISO's CSV into one national map. TWO HAZARDS FOUND AND ROUTED, NEITHER CAUSED BY THIS LANE AND NEITHER TOUCHED. (1) Re-deriving PJM's or MISO's coal supply CSV at HEAD with NO CODE CHANGE AT ALL already re-ranks 5 PJM plants (594, 876, 879, 3149, 6166) and 10 MISO plants (1082, 1091, 1733, 2107, 4041, 4078, 6034, 7343, 8023, 56068), because the raw f923_*.zip receipt corpus their committed CSVs were built from is no longer under data/raw and the generation fallback disagrees with it. SPP is the clean case (every row source=generation). No ISO may re-derive without reconciling that lost source first; recorded in data/raw/_processed-legacy/README.md. (2) coal_supply_*.csv is a solve-affecting registry table that the capx D79 solve-surface fingerprint does NOT cover (the surface is seven config MODULES) and that carries no resolved_inputs sha256 stamp the way campd-unit-outages-SPP.csv and thermal_tranches_SPP.csv do -- harmless here because inertness is proven by direct measurement, but a real hole stated rather than relied on. Each is another desk's card (rule 28(d)).
